opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only for the role that owns the system, so write is the maximum here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB lists E024 as a contractor with basic training (HR note said full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type). Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Employee E024 requested write access to Source Code. The Security note identifies E024 as a contractor with basic security training, and states the Security DB is authoritative for employment type (HR note claimed full-time, which conflicts). Per policy, contractors max out at read unless they have advanced security training (basic training here, so no write). The requested write exceeds the maximum of read, so grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Donna Ball (E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR note: role Payroll Specialist, full_time, recommends write for Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code (Engineer does), so write is the max. Recommend write.
- Security note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor (Security DB authoritative), basic training. Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.

So there's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor and claims Security DB is authoritative for employment type.

Policy:
1. full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic training, max is read. Requested write > read, grant read.

If full-time, max is write, grant write (requested write).

Which to use? The Security note says Security DB is authoritative for employment type. The HR note says looked up in own database. Hmm.

The Approver must decide. The notes provide conflicting facts. Security says its DB is authoritative for employment type. I'll go with the security note: contractor, basic training → max read. Grant read since requested write is above max.

Actually, let me think carefully. The team memory has two notes. The Approver reads the notes and makes the final decision. The conflict is employment type. Security agent explicitly says its database is authoritative for employment type. So I should trust contractor status. Therefore max = read.

Submit decision: read.
